title: Linear Algebra for Modeling & Robotics
description: Vectors, matrices, eigenstructure, least squares, and linear transformations applied to state estimation, circuit networks, and robot coordinates.

outcomes.description: Solve linear systems and diagnose singularity.
Interpret bases, rank, and null spaces.
Use eigenvalues to describe linear dynamics.
Fit an overdetermined model by least squares.

lesson_objectives.description: Interpret pivots and rank as information about solutions.
Distinguish a geometric vector from its coordinates in a basis.
Interpret eigenvalues of a transition matrix.
Derive normal equations for a full-rank linear model.
Interpret residuals and avoid overclaiming from fit quality.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Linear systems, elimination, and rank
lessons.worked_example: The system x+y=3, 2x+2y=6 has rank 1 and infinitely many solutions; the second equation adds no independent constraint.

modules.title: Vector spaces, bases, and coordinate transforms

lessons.title: Vector spaces, bases, and coordinate transforms
lessons.worked_example: A 90° planar rotation maps (1,0) to (0,1); the vector's coordinates change because its orientation changes relative to the frame.

lessons.title: Eigenvalues and linear dynamical systems
lessons.worked_example: For ẋ=−2x, the solution decays as e^(−2t), with time constant 0.5 in the chosen time unit.

lessons.title: Least squares and data fitting
lessons.worked_example: For observations y=[1,3] at x=[0,2], the least-squares line has slope 1 and intercept 1, fitting both points exactly.
